headline: Ancelotti: I was saving Neymar for extra-time in Japan clash
summary: Brazil's coach explains why the star forward remained on the bench during their dramatic 2-1 comeback win over Japan.
details: Brazil secured a dramatic 2-1 comeback victory over Japan in the FIFA World Cup Round of 32, keeping their hopes for a sixth title alive.
Despite the win, many fans were surprised that Neymar, Brazil's all-time leading scorer, remained on the bench for the entire match.
Coach Carlo Ancelotti clarified that he was saving Neymar for extra-time, stating he would have entered the pitch in the 105th minute if Brazil hadn't scored their winning goal.
The match began poorly for Brazil as Kaishu Sano scored for Japan in the 29th minute after intercepting a misplaced pass from Danilo.
Brazil struggled to break through Japan's organized defense for much of the first half, facing a defensive masterclass from the 'Samurai Blue'.
The comeback started in the 56th minute when Casemiro headed in a cross from Gabriel Magalhaes to equalize the score.
The drama peaked in the 95th minute when Gabriel Martinelli scored a late winner from a pass by Bruno Guimaraes, sealing the victory in normal time.
Brazil now advances to the round of 16, where they will face either Norway or Ivory Coast in New Jersey on Sunday.
caption:
Why was Neymar on the bench? Ancelotti reveals the plan for Brazil's star man during their nail-biting win over Japan.

Brazil secured a dramatic 2-1 comeback victory over Japan in the FIFA World Cup Round of 32, keeping their hopes for a sixth title alive.

Despite the win, many fans were surprised that Neymar, Brazil's all-time leading scorer, remained on the bench for the entire match.

Coach Carlo Ancelotti clarified that he was saving Neymar for extra-time, stating he would have entered the pitch in the 105th minute if Brazil hadn't scored their winning goal.

The match began poorly for Brazil as Kaishu Sano scored for Japan in the 29th minute after intercepting a misplaced pass from Danilo.

Brazil struggled to break through Japan's organized defense for much of the first half, facing a defensive masterclass from the 'Samurai Blue'.

The comeback started in the 56th minute when Casemiro headed in a cross from Gabriel Magalhaes to equalize the score.

The drama peaked in the 95th minute when Gabriel Martinelli scored a late winner from a pass by Bruno Guimaraes, sealing the victory in normal time.

Brazil now advances to the round of 16, where they will face either Norway or Ivory Coast in New Jersey on Sunday.
